title: Transactions and ACID

spans.text: “Transactions and ACID” is a tool for solving a concrete programming problem. Identify the input and desired result, then trace what role the construct plays in the example. Study it not only as syntax, but also for its effects on readability, correctness, resource use, and future changes.
QUESTION: What will this example do? Predict the result first.
Both updates are committed together in the same transaction.

A transaction groups several writes into one logical unit. COMMIT accepts the changes; ROLLBACK cancels the transaction's changes. ACID describes atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability. For example, debiting one account and crediting another must succeed together.

Key line: `BEGIN;`
What it does: Both updates are committed together in the same transaction.
Why it is used: Keep transactions short, check errors, and make the application's commit/rollback policy explicit.
If omitted or changed: Isolation levels and locking differ by engine; SQLite and PostgreSQL do not have identical concurrency models.

spans.title: Common mistake
spans.text: Roll back on failure before commit; a partial change may violate a business rule.
